html:
Pedro Albizu Campos was the leader of the Puerto Rican Nationalist Party from 1930 and the most famous champion of independence from the United States. He spent about 25 years in prison.

A graduate of Harvard Law School who had served in the US Army, he argued that US rule over Puerto Rico was illegal. His party turned to armed struggle after the Ponce massacre of 1937.

In 1950 nationalists rose in several towns, including Jayuya, and attacked the governor's mansion; others tried to kill President Truman in Washington. In 1954 nationalists shot at members of Congress. Albizu was jailed again and released, gravely ill, in 1964. He is honoured by supporters of independence as the heir of the Grito de Lares, though Munoz Marin's path won most voters.
